messages.author: 9194f713a01c3ddf
messages.subject: RODBC Crashes Shiny Server
parts:
So we've been struggling with this for a few days now and haven't made any progress on a solution. Below is the description of out problem:

We are running a Shiny Server (and Shiny Dashboard) on RedHat 6.7 (R version 3.2.2 Fire Safety) and have been running into a segfault when trying to query a database using RODBC. This happens when we source the file into app.R or make a query request to the database in the server.R file. When we run the same code in the R console it works just fine.

It seems like there must be some type of interaction between Shiny and RODBC that is causing this issue. As a workaround we are using the RJDBC, which works fine, but we're worried it isn't going to scale well for us. And it's quite slow.

Anyone have an idea what we can do to make RODBC work correctly?

If you would like more details you can see the SO post I made yesterday. I'm sorry to double posting but after searching far and wide we haven't found any helpful information.

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/34316243/rodbc-query-brings-down-shiny-server

Thanks!


-C

messages.subject: Re: RODBC Crashes Shiny Server
parts:

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: RODBC Crashes Shiny Server
parts:
Where in the server.R are you making the query?

And also, does it help if you add the bolded line?

myConn <- odbcConnect("DSN_Name")
segment <- sqlQuery(myConn, "SELECT * FROM foo")
odbcClose(myConn)
(ideally that close call should be in a tryCatch/finally or on.exit to make sure it closes even if an error occurs, but it's hard to know which to do without knowing where this code is going...)

parts:
First of all, I'd like to thank Joe Cheng. He was a massive help and really went out of his way to help me resolve this issue. Thanks a ton.

So the issue that I ran into was the result of poor code structure. Here were the mistakes I made and once they were fixed things worked as expected.
  • Mistake 1 - I was calling the server.R file app.R. This is an outdated naming convention and shouldn't be used.
  • Mistake 2 - The last line of my server.R file called the function shinyApp(ui, server). This was causing major issues with my odbc driver to my database. It was creating a very large stack where my client would be pushed too far down and result in a seg fault. Moral of the story, end your server.R file with the server function. Here are some examples of ways to do this correctly (Joe shared these examples with me):

    server <- function(input, output, session) {

      ...

    }

    server

     

    Or:

     

    function(input, output, session) {

      ...

    }

     

    Or:

     

    shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

      ...

    })


My shiny server is now happily running! : )


Thanks to Joe for all the help.



-c

messages.subject: Re: RODBC Crashes Shiny Server
parts:
Just a very small clarification. app.R and server.R are both perfectly valid and up-to-date, but they are used in different ways.

app.R is used when you want a single file to contain both ui and server parts of your app; and the last thing in an app.R must be a call to shinyApp(ui, server) (or technically, it could be some other expression that returns a shinyApp object, but in the end a shinyApp object must be returned).

server.R is used to define only the server portion, because your UI is defined somewhere else (either ui.R or www/index.html). In this case, you just need to make sure that nothing appears after your shinyServer(function(input, output, session) { ... }).

For 99% of apps the two approaches are equivalent, you can simply pick whichever one suits your personal preferences. Some people like to keep the UI and server logic separated from each other, some like to keep them together.
